Spellthreads are tailor-crafted augments that grant caster-class bonuses to leg armor. Like other augments, applying a thread will overwrite another augment or enchant on the item. The Burning Crusade expansion is required for a tailor to craft spellthreads, but non-BC players can buy and use the threads on their equipment. Most tailors will only be able to craft 2 of the 4 available threads, because they must choose between Aldor or Scryers. Wrath of the Lich King expansion introduced several additional spellthread patterns.

Spell penetration reduces the target's resistance to your spells; it is a different mechanic from spell hit rating. Spell penetration only works against targets with resistances, and will not reduce resistances below zero. Spell penetration typically is a PvP stat, intended to help casters against players who wear resistance gear or are buffed with extra resistance, such as Mark of the Wild. In PvE, targets of a higher level than the caster have a base resistance (2% of mitigation per level difference) which cannot be overcome by spell penetration nor by any other stat. Otherwise, very few mobs and raid-level bosses have a substantial amount of resistance to overcome.

Bonuses for spell penetration can be found on blue, green, and purple gems, but the currently provides penetration as well. This is believed to have been an error in its itemization, but Blizzard has thus far made no mention of fixing it, which makes it a valuable gem for filling yellow sockets in PvP gear for DoT-based casters (who do not typically care about spell crit and may prefer spell penetration to intellect).

Speedbarge Diving Helm is a buff rewarded when accepting Down in the Deeps at Fizzle and Pozzik's Speedbarge. Similar to Sea Legs, the buff provides underwater walking, water-breathing and a movement speed increase while underwater in Thousand Needles. After the quest, players will always have this buff in Thousand Needles. The speed bonus depends on how the player is moving: * Swimming speed is increased by 60%, becoming roughly 8% faster than running on land. * Running on the sea floor is as fast as apprentice riding on land at 60% faster than running on land. * The buff does not stack with Mounts.

Sphere of Suppression is an Azerite Essence obtained through battlegrounds. This essence can only be used by tank specializations.

The Sphere of Suppressed Force is a quest reward from Storming the Battlefields. Only classes with a tank specialization can receive it. For characters who chose the Azerite-Encrusted Timequartz or Roiling Blood of the Vanquished when completing Storming the Battlefields, this item can be purchased for 5 Mark of Honor from in Boralus or in Zuldazar. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 1 of the Sphere of Suppression Essence and leave behind a Split Sphere.

The Sphere of Unrestrained Fury can be purchased for 25 Mark of Honor from in Boralus or in Zuldazar after completing Battlefield Brawler. For characters who have already learned Rank 2 of Artifice of Time or Blood of the Enemy, its cost is lowered to 10 Mark of Honor. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 2 of the Sphere of Suppression Essence and leave behind a Split Sphere.

The Sphere of Leeched Mobility can be purchased for 25 Mark of Honor from in Boralus or in Zuldazar after completing Battlefield Tactician. For characters who have already learned Rank 3 of Artifice of Time or Blood of the Enemy, its cost is lowered to 10 Mark of Honor. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 3 of the Sphere of Suppression Essence and leave behind a Split Sphere.

The Sphere of Incandescent Neutralization could be purchased for 25 Mark of Honor from in Boralus or in Zuldazar after completing Battlefield Master. For characters who had already learned Rank 4 of Artifice of Time or Blood of the Enemy, its cost was lowered to 10 Mark of Honor. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 4 of the Sphere of Suppression Essence and leave behind a Split Sphere.

.]] Spirit Healers are angelic beings usually encountered at a graveyard after death. These floating figures of death and rebirth return people to life where their spirit stands. The Spirit Healers are Watchers, kyrian whose role is to eternally evaluate souls within the Veil. They are called to those who die to peer into the soul's inner self and evaluate whether they are ready to be dead. If the Watchers deem the soul ready, they will call forth a kyrian Bearer to come and bring their soul to the Shadowlands. If they aren't ready, the Watchers return them to life.

The Spirestone Battle Lord is a rare mob ogre found in Lower Blackrock Spire. He spawns on the hill next to Highlord Omokk, leader of the Spirestone tribe. His most common drops are Swiftdart Battleboots and The Blackrock Slicer. While The Blackrock Slicer may not be the best axe based on statistics, it is often considered one of the coolest looking.

The Spirestone Butcher is a rare mob ogre found in Lower Blackrock Spire. He patrols in the hallway leading to Highlord Omokk, leader of the Spirestone tribe. Because he patrols alone, as long as you've cleared the first three ogres you'll see as you come down from the main instance entrance, he's an easy fight. If you're not careful, he can become an add to that first three-ogre fight, making him more challenging. He hits hard but goes down quickly.
As this returns mana (or rage) when you kill a target, is is mostly of use to characters in a damage dealing role than those in healing or tanking roles.
The Spirestone Lord Magus is an ogre residing in Lower Blackrock Spire. He spawns on the hill next to Highlord Omokk, leader of the Spirestone tribe.
Spined Crawlers are crabs found in the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale. Tyrande Whisperwind killed several of them on her way to reclaim Darkshore during the Fourth War.
Spiked Stegodon are stegodons found at Terror Run in Un'Goro Crater.
The Spirit Den is a hidden cave located on the north side of Mistvale Valley. There, you can find Witch Doctor Unbagwa for the quest Stranglethorn Fever.

Spigot Operator Luglunket of the Gadgetzan Water Company, is a goblin quest giver located in Gadgetzan in Tanaris. He has been missing since the Cataclysm, possibly having become one of the many victims of the great Tanaris tsunami.

Spider crabs (or spidercrabs and spine crabs) are a type of crabs. The spider crabs in Nazjatar tend to inhabit dark caverns, hiding in the shadows. Their population may increase on occasion, but luckily snapdragons have developed a taste for their roe, and the Unshackled use the crabs' spines for projectiles. They originally appeared in Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne as Sunken Ruins creeps, and were reintroduced in Battle for Azeroth in Nazjatar with a new appearance.
Spire Spiderlings are crystal spiders found in Blackrock Spire. They are also spawned when killing Spire Spiders and Mother Smolderweb.

Spike is a darkhound critter, being chased by Underfoot around the Blacksmith in Arathi Basin. Spike and Underfoot appear only when the Blacksmith is claimed by the Horde for the Defilers. The Alliance counterpart of Spike is Cleo who is chased by Lady when the League of Arathor controls the Blacksmith.

Spinebreaker Pass is a straight but narrow chasm located in the far southeastern Hellfire Peninsula. It is a safe way for Horde to travel between Zeth'Gor and the Legion Front via Void Ridge without having to sneak past the Alliance forces at Expedition Point. Alliance players can also use the pass to access Void Ridge without having to cross through the Legion Front, as there are no Horde-aligned npcs of any kind in the pass, despite its name.
